**Defects found:**

1. **Mutable default argument (`seen=[]`)** — The default list is created once, at function definition time, and reused across every call that doesn't pass `seen` explicitly. Since the function mutates it (`seen.append(...)`), scores from one call will "leak" into subsequent calls, causing previously-seen values to be silently excluded from `result` in later, unrelated invocations. This is a classic Python footgun and will produce incorrect/inconsistent results depending on call history.

2. **`IndexError` when `len(scores) < limit`** — The loop does `for i in range(0, limit)` and indexes `scores[i]` unconditionally. If `scores` has fewer than `limit` elements, this raises an `IndexError` instead of just returning however many scores are available.

3. **Duplicate values within `scores` collapse silently, shrinking the result below `limit`** — The `seen` list (whether freshly empty or, worse, polluted per defect #1) causes any repeated value within the same `scores` list to be skipped after its first occurrence. So `top_scores([90, 90, 80, 70, 60], limit=5)` returns only 4 results (`[90, 80, 70, 60]`) instead of 5, even though there were enough elements. This may or may not be intended ("top N distinct scores"), but combined with defect #1 it's clearly buggy since it also drops values that were never in this call's input at all.

4. **`ZeroDivisionError` on empty `scores`** — `average = sum(scores) / len(scores)` will throw if `scores` is an empty list, since `len(scores)` is 0.

5. **In-place mutation of the caller's list (`scores.sort(reverse=True)`)** — Sorting is done in place on the caller-supplied list rather than on a copy. This silently reorders the caller's original data as a side effect, which can surprise callers who didn't expect their input list to be mutated.

No other issues are present — the descending sort and the "average of all scores" calculation are correctly implemented as intended.
